successCriteria.description: IPolicyService exposes a method (e.g. listEffectivePolicies(asOf: Date)) that returns at most one policy per leaveTypeCode — the one with status ACTIVE, effectiveFrom <= asOf, and (effectiveTo is null OR effectiveTo >= asOf); when multiple rows still match a code, the one with the latest effectiveFrom wins. It must be built on the existing IPolicyRepository.findAll (no new repository method).

IBalanceService gains getBalanceForEmployee(employeeId) returning a LIST (array) of balance entries — never a single object — one entry per effective leave-type policy for the caller's CURRENT accrual period. Each entry carries leaveTypeCode, periodStart, periodEnd, entitledDays, usedDays, pendingDays, and a computed available = entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays.

getBalanceForEmployee derives each leave type's current period via the shared periodContaining(employee.hireDate, policy.accrualPeriodMonths, new Date()) and looks the balance up with findByKey using period.start/period.end mapped to periodStart/periodEnd. It is read-only: no uow.withTransaction, no writes, no client forwarded.

A leave type with an effective policy but no balance row for the current period does NOT throw NotFoundError and does NOT fail the whole request — the implementation consistently either omits that type or returns it zero-filled, and applies that choice uniformly across all types.

balance.routes.ts registers a route that resolves the actor from request.user (never a client-supplied id) via a resolveActor helper matching leave.routes.ts, calls getBalanceForEmployee(actor.id), and maps errors via a sendError helper matching leave.routes.ts (AppError -> { error, code } with correct status; other -> 500).
src/modules/balance/index.ts exports balanceRoutes (in addition to the existing model/repository/service exports).

constraints: Read-only operation: getBalanceForEmployee must not open a transaction (no uow.withTransaction), must not write, and must not forward a PoolClient to findByKey.

The effective-policy listing must be built on the existing IPolicyRepository.findAll (unfiltered) and filtered in the service — do NOT add a repository method, do NOT touch the leave-type module, and do NOT add a balance -> leave-type dependency (the committed dependency map is balance -> policy).
The actor identity must come from request.user only; never accept a client-supplied employee id.
No tests in this sub-phase (they land in a later phase).
outOfScope: src/shared/date/accrual.ts and the LeaveService refactor to consume it (sibling Sub-phase 3a).
Unit tests and smoke-check assertions for the balance read endpoint (later phase).
Adding any repository method or a balance -> leave-type module dependency.

entityInvariants.invariant: At most one policy is in effect per leaveTypeCode at any given date: status ACTIVE, effectiveFrom <= asOf, and (effectiveTo is null OR effectiveTo >= asOf); if multiple rows still match, the latest effectiveFrom is the single effective policy.

A balance entry is identified by (employeeId, leaveTypeCode, periodStart, periodEnd); the current-period balance for a leave type is looked up via findByKey with the period derived from periodContaining(hireDate, accrualPeriodMonths, now).

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns an array (possibly empty); never throws for an empty result. Filtering is mandatory (ACTIVE + effective window + latest effectiveFrom tiebreak).
Returns a list (never a single object). A type with an effective policy but no balance row must not throw NotFoundError. Read-only: no transaction, no writes.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Authenticated only (not in PUBLIC_PATHS); actor resolved from request.user via resolveActor; UnauthorizedError on missing/invalid actor.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: AppError -> { error, code } with correct status; any other throw -> 500.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Reuse the shared periodContaining (and its start/end output) for accrual-period derivation — do not re-implement period arithmetic in the balance service.
Match the resolveActor and sendError helper behavior (actor from request.user, role validation, AppError -> { error, code }, other -> 500) exactly as leave.routes.ts.
Use the existing IPolicyRepository.findAll (unfiltered) as the data source for effective-policy listing; do not add a repository method.
Look up balances via the existing findByKey(employeeId, leaveTypeCode, periodStart, periodEnd) signature, mapping periodContaining's { start, end } to periodStart/periodEnd.
Resolve the employee (for hireDate) via the existing IEmployeeService.getEmployeeById.
The available computation must equal entitledDays - usedDays - pendingDays, matching the canonical sufficiency formula used by the validation module.

integrationPoints.why: Provides the effective-policy listing (accrualPeriodMonths + leaveTypeCode) that drives the per-type balance lookup.
Supplies the employee's hireDate used as the accrual anchor.
Single source of truth for deriving the current accrual period.
Reads the current-period balance row for each effective leave type.
